newsitem.title: USA: Navistar to close foundry, take Q4 charge.
newsitem.headline: Navistar to close foundry, take Q4 charge.

text.p: Navistar International Corp said on Tuesday it will close its Indianapolis Casting Corp foundry in late 1998.
The truckmaker said it will take an unspecified charge in the fourth quarter on the closing of the plant, which employs 650 people.

The company said that on Sunday an extension of its master contract was ratified by 63 percent of its voting United Auto Workers union members. It takes effect immediately and runs through October 1, 2002, Navistar said.
About 8,000 employees in Springfield, Ohio, Indianapolis, Ft. Wayne, Ind., Melrose Park, Ill., and other locations are represented by the UAW, the company said.
Navistar chief executive John Horne said, "We are well on the road to renewal, and this contract is a major milestone."
UAW international vice president Jack Laskowski said, "I am very pleased with the positive vote on the master contract, and with the work done in Springfield to create a brighter future there."

Under the agreement, Navistar said it will proceed with a five-point strategy including plans to focus its Springfield, Ohio, assembly plant on production of medium-duty trucks. Heavy models being made in Springfield will be moved to other facilities, the company said, adding that its next generation truck will be built in Springfield.

On Sunday, local UAW members at Navistar's Indianapolis Casting Corp, or ICC, foundry rejected a proposal that the company said "would have kept the foundry cost competitive and financially viable in the face of foreign competition."
As a result, Navistar said it would proceed with plans to close ICC in late 1998. The company said it has invested heavily at the foundry in recent years, making it more productive and efficient.

"With wage levels 50 percent higher than the competition's, however, ICC could no longer stay competitive without a new labor agreement, particularly in the face of future competition from foundries in Latin America, where labor costs are significantly lower," Navistar said.
The foundry's 650 employees make grey-iron castings for engines, Navistar said.
"The decision to close ICC will result in a charge to fourth-quarter earnings," said the Chicago-based company.
